```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "Setup: read the caches"
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
# Code is shown (folded) in the HTML version and hidden in the PDF.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = knitr::is_html_output())
options(knitr.kable.NA = "—")
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)

cache = readRDS(file.path("data", "io-yft-age-k-cache.rds"))
truth = readRDS(file.path("data", "io-yft-sim-truth-cache.rds"))
ss3   = cache$ss3
S     = cache$summary
truth_traj = truth$total[, .(ts, ssb, static_dep)]

lab = c(A1      = "opal A1: endgrowth biology, SS3 selectivity",
        A2      = "opal A2: control biology, SS3 selectivity",
        C       = "opal C: endgrowth biology, opal selectivity",
        C2      = "opal C2: as C, prior-dominated parameters fixed",
        schnute = "opal, Schnute growth (earlier vignette)",
        ss3     = "SS3",
        truth   = "Simulated truth")
col = setNames(c("#C0392B", "#2471A3", "#1E8449", "#8E44AD", "#A6ACAF", "grey20", "#D4AC0D"), lab)
lty = setNames(c("solid", "dashed", "solid", "dashed", "dotted", "solid", "solid"), lab)
scale_series = list(scale_colour_manual(values = col, name = NULL),
                    scale_linetype_manual(values = lty, name = NULL))
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
          theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))

fleet_name = function(f) {
    f  = as.integer(f)
    nm = c(cache$fleet_names[1:16], paste0("llcpue_q", 1:4))
    sprintf("%d: %s", f, nm[f])
}
fmt = function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
sci = function(x, d = 1) formatC(x, format = "e", digits = d)
term = function(dt, v) dt[ts == max(ts)][[v]]

# Fitted trajectories with SS3, the truth and the earlier Schnute fit
tr  = cache$trajectory[state == "fitted"]
sch = cache$schnute$trajectory[route == "endgrowth"]
all_traj = rbind(
    tr[, .(ts, ssb, static_dep, series = lab[id])],
    sch[, .(ts, ssb, static_dep, series = lab["schnute"])],
    ss3$trajectory[, .(ts, ssb, static_dep, series = lab["ss3"])],
    truth_traj[, .(ts, ssb, static_dep, series = lab["truth"])])
vs = function(x, ref) {
    m = merge(x[, .(ts, ssb, static_dep)], ref[, .(ts, r_ssb = ssb, r_dep = static_dep)], by = "ts")
    m[, .(mean_abs_pct = mean(abs(100 * (ssb / r_ssb - 1))),
          max_abs_pct  = max(abs(100 * (ssb / r_ssb - 1))),
          terminal_pct = 100 * (ssb[ts == max(ts)] / r_ssb[ts == max(ts)] - 1),
          terminal_dep = static_dep[ts == max(ts)],
          max_dep_err  = max(abs(static_dep - r_dep)))]
}
```

# Overview

This vignette follows
[*SS3 to opal: IO yellowfin*](ss3-to-opal-io-yft.html), which converted the
Indian Ocean yellowfin SS3 model into opal and compared fits. The SS3 model,
the baseline here, was built by the IATTC analyst team (Mark N. Maunder,
Haikun Xu and Carolina Minte-Vera) for the Spatial Stock Assessment
Simulation Experiment; see **Credit**. That comparison
found that fitted opal models diverged from SS3 because of growth. SS3 uses
`GrowthModel 3`, with age-specific K, and opal's single-k Schnute curve
could not represent it. It was 5 to 16 cm too long at ages 4–8, which shifted
every predicted length composition. A local patch supplying SS3's
length-at-age confirmed the diagnosis.

opal 0.1.1 (`dev` branch, commit `c493461`) implements age-specific K as an
option to `get_growth()`.
**The method is Stock Synthesis'**: cumulative K multipliers, Linf derived
from the oldest-age K, and SS3's plus-group length approximation (Methot and
Wetzel 2013; SS3 source, `SS_Label_Info_16.2.2`–`16.2.4.1.4`). This vignette
uses it with the growth parameters read from the SS3 files, so no patch is
needed. It then goes one step further than the first vignette, and lets opal
estimate its own selectivity.

**Key results.**

* opal's length-at-age now equals SS3's to Report.sso print precision: max
  relative error `r sci(max(abs(cache$growth$laa_opal / cache$growth$laa_ss3 - 1)))`
  over ages 1–28.
* **A1**, with SS3's selectivity: B0 is
  `r fmt(S[id == "A1", B0_fit] / ss3$ssb0, 2)` × SS3's and terminal depletion
  is `r fmt(term(tr[id == "A1"], "static_dep"), 3)`, against SS3's
  `r fmt(term(ss3$trajectory, "static_dep"), 3)`. With Schnute growth the
  same configuration gave `r fmt(cache$schnute$summary[route == "endgrowth", B0_fit] / ss3$ssb0, 2)` ×
  and `r fmt(term(sch, "static_dep"), 3)`.
* **A2**, with control-file biology through opal's PLA, now sits close to A1:
  B0 `r fmt(S[id == "A2", B0_fit] / ss3$ssb0, 2)` × SS3's (with Schnute growth,
  `r fmt(cache$schnute$summary[route == "control", B0_fit] / ss3$ssb0, 2)` ×).
* **C** estimates the opal equivalents of the
  `r S[id == "C", n_par_sel]` selectivity parameters SS3 estimated. B0 is
  `r fmt(S[id == "C", B0_fit] / ss3$ssb0, 2)` × SS3's and terminal depletion
  `r fmt(term(tr[id == "C"], "static_dep"), 3)`. Opal check:
  `r if (S[id == "C", check_passes]) "passed" else "**failed**"`. Nine of
  those parameters are set by opal's selectivity prior rather than the data.
* **C2** fixes those nine at their seeded values and estimates the other
  `r S[id == "C2", n_par_sel]`: B0 `r fmt(S[id == "C2", B0_fit] / ss3$ssb0, 2)` ×
  SS3's, terminal depletion `r fmt(term(tr[id == "C2"], "static_dep"), 3)`.
  Opal check: `r if (S[id == "C2", check_passes]) "passed" else "**failed**"`.
* Against the simulated truth (terminal depletion
  `r fmt(term(truth_traj, "static_dep"), 3)`), see section 8.

| Step | File | Does |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `case-studies/io-yft/scripts/01-fit-io-yft-ss3-opal.r` | Earlier fits; supplies the SS3 reference quantities and the Schnute-growth reference lines |
| 2 | `case-studies/io-yft/scripts/02-extract-io-yft-sim-truth.r` | Simulated truth cache |
| 3 | `case-studies/io-yft/scripts/03-fit-io-yft-age-k.r` | The fits in this vignette; writes `vignettes/data/io-yft-age-k-cache.rds` |
| 4 | `case-studies/io-yft/vignettes/ss3-to-opal-io-yft-age-k.qmd` | This document; reads only the caches |

The cache was written `r cache$created` with R `r cache$session$r`, opal
`r cache$session$opal` and r4ss `r cache$session$r4ss`.

# SS3 growth in opal

With `growth.model: ss3_age_k` in the converter config, every growth input is
read from the SS3 files. Nothing is fitted.

```{r}
#| label: growth-spec
g = cache$growth
knitr::kable(data.table(
    input = c("L1 (L_at_Amin, age 1)", "L2 (L_at_Amax, age 28)",
              "k per quarter (VonBert_K / 4)", "K multiplier ages", "K multipliers",
              "CV1, CV2 (CV_young, CV_old)", "plus-group adjustment"),
    value = c(fmt(g$L1, 1), fmt(g$L2, 1), fmt(g$k_per_step, 5),
              paste(g$k_mult_ages, collapse = ", "), paste(g$k_mult, collapse = ", "),
              paste(fmt(c(g$CV1, g$CV2), 2), collapse = ", "), "yes")))
```

SS3 reads K as an annual rate and applies it over the 3-month season, so
opal's per-step k is K / 4. M is scaled the same way. The multipliers are
cumulative: K at an age is the previous age's K times that age's multiplier.

```{r}
#| label: growth-curve
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Mean length-at-age: SS3, opal with SS3 age-specific K, and the single-k Schnute curve used previously."
schnute_laa = readRDS(file.path("data", "io-yft-ss3-opal-cache.rds"))$biology[route == "endgrowth", length_opal]
gc = rbind(data.table(age = seq_along(g$laa_ss3),  length = g$laa_ss3,  series = "SS3 (Len_Beg)"),
           data.table(age = seq_along(g$laa_opal), length = g$laa_opal, series = "opal, SS3 age-specific K"),
           data.table(age = seq_along(schnute_laa), length = schnute_laa, series = "opal, Schnute (earlier)"))
ggplot(gc, aes(age, length, colour = series, linetype = series)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("SS3 (Len_Beg)" = "grey20", "opal, SS3 age-specific K" = "#C0392B",
                                   "opal, Schnute (earlier)" = "#A6ACAF"), name = NULL) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c("SS3 (Len_Beg)" = "solid", "opal, SS3 age-specific K" = "dashed",
                                     "opal, Schnute (earlier)" = "dotted"), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Age (quarters)", y = "Mean length (cm)")
```

```{r}
#| label: growth-table
knitr::kable(data.table(age = seq_along(g$laa_ss3), ss3 = g$laa_ss3, opal = g$laa_opal,
                        diff = g$laa_opal - g$laa_ss3)[age %in% c(1:10, 15, 20, 25, 28)],
             digits = c(0, 4, 4, 5),
             col.names = c("Age", "SS3 Len_Beg (cm)", "opal (cm)", "opal − SS3 (cm)"))
```

The SD of length-at-age is CV × length with CV1 = CV2 = 0.1, the same as
SS3's `SD_Beg`. With growth exact, opal's probability-of-length-at-age matrix
(PLA) is SS3's age-length key at the start of the timestep.

# Configurations

| Fit | Biology | Selectivity | Estimated |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A1** | endgrowth (SS3 age vectors) | SS3 selectivity-at-age, fixed | log B0, 256 rec devs, 4 q |
| **A2** | control file, through the PLA | SS3 selectivity-at-age, fixed | as A1 |
| **C** | endgrowth | opal length-based curves | as A1, plus `r S[id == "C", n_par_sel]` selectivity parameters |
| **C2** | endgrowth | as C | as A1, plus `r S[id == "C2", n_par_sel]` selectivity parameters (nine of C's held at seeded values) |

All four fix growth at SS3's values, and steepness and σ_R at SS3's. They
start from the converted SS3 optimum. The length compositions enter as
multinomials with SS3's `mult_by_lencomp_N` variance adjustments.

## Selectivity in fit C

Fit C estimates the opal equivalents of exactly the selectivity parameters
SS3 estimated (positive phase in `control.ss_new`):

```{r}
#| label: sel-params
# One row per SS3 selectivity parameter: fleet (S1 is the survey, fleet 17),
# parameter number, value and phase.
sp = copy(ss3$age_selex_parms)
sp[, fleet := ifelse(grepl("_S1$", parameter), 17L,
                     as.integer(sub(".*_FL([0-9]+)$", "\\1", parameter)))]
sp[, p := as.integer(sub("^AgeSel_[0-9]+P_([0-9]+)_.*", "\\1", parameter))]
est = sp[, .(estimated = paste0("P", sort(p[phase > 0]), collapse = ", "),
             fixed     = paste(sprintf("P%d = %g", p[phase <= 0], value[phase <= 0]), collapse = "; ")),
         by = fleet]
# Fleets 1-14 share one pattern; check before collapsing them into one row.
stopifnot(uniqueN(est[fleet <= 14, .(estimated, fixed)]) == 1L)
knitr::kable(data.table(
    ss3_fleet = c("1–14", "15, 16", "17 (survey)"),
    pattern   = c("20 (double-normal)", "15 (mirror fleet 14)", "12 (logistic)"),
    estimated = c(est[fleet == 1, estimated], "—", est[fleet == 17, estimated]),
    fixed     = c(est[fleet == 1, fixed], "—", est[fleet == 17, fixed]),
    opal      = c("double-normal; columns 1–4 estimated, 5–6 at seeded values",
                  "share fishery 14's parameters",
                  "logistic; both estimated, shared by opal index fisheries 17–20")),
    col.names = c("SS3 fleet", "SS3 pattern", "SS3 estimated", "SS3 fixed", "opal equivalent"))
```

SS3's double normal (pattern 20) and opal's take their six parameters in the
same order, so SS3's P1–P4 map to opal columns 1–4. The initial and final
values (columns 5–6) stay at their seeded values. opal has no equivalent of
SS3's `−999` final-value option, so the seeded value stands in for it.
Starting values come from fitting each opal curve to SS3's selectivity
projected onto length (seeding RMSE ≤ `r fmt(max(cache$seed_rmse), 3)`),
within opal's default bounds of [−7, 7]. opal's default N(0, 2) prior on
`par_sel` applies. The survey curve has less information in opal than in SS3,
because SS3 also fitted the survey's generalised size-composition data, which
the converter omits.

# Conversion checks

```{r}
#| label: reconcile
rc = cache$reconcile[id == "A1" & !grepl("^catch total", quantity),
                     .(quantity, rel_diff = signif(rel_diff, 3),
                       tol = ifelse(is.na(tol), "", sci(tol, 0)), pass)]
knitr::kable(rc)
```

The 16 catch totals reconcile exactly too (not shown). The growth row is new:
with SS3's own growth form, length-at-age is now an exact check rather than
an approximation. The SPR0 tolerance allows for SS3's truncated plus-group
equilibrium, as explained in the first vignette.

# Optimisation

As before, **every fit starts from the converted SS3 optimum, so these times
are for refining a solution that is already close**. Fit C also starts from
seeded selectivity curves.

```{r}
#| label: timing
tm = dcast(cache$timing, stage ~ id, value.var = "seconds")
tm = tm[match(unique(cache$timing$stage), stage)]
tm = rbind(tm, tm[, lapply(.SD, sum, na.rm = TRUE), .SDcols = c("A1", "A2", "C", "C2")][, stage := "total"],
           fill = TRUE)
knitr::kable(tm[, .(stage, A1, A2, C, C2)], digits = 1,
             col.names = c("Stage", "A1 (s)", "A2 (s)", "C (s)", "C2 (s)"))
```

```{r}
#| label: optimiser
knitr::kable(cache$optimiser[, .(id, pass, objective = round(objective, 3), convergence,
                                 iterations, fn_evals, gr_evals)],
             col.names = c("Fit", "Pass", "Objective", "Convergence", "Iterations",
                           "Function evals", "Gradient evals"))
knitr::kable(S[, .(id, n_par, n_par_sel, objective_start = round(objective_start, 1),
                   objective_fit = round(objective_fit, 1))],
             col.names = c("Fit", "Parameters", "Selectivity parameters",
                           "Objective, start", "Objective, fit"))
knitr::kable(S[, .(id, grad_nlminb = sci(max_gradient_nlminb), grad_final = sci(max_gradient),
                   newton_steps, check = ifelse(check_passes, "passed", "failed"),
                   estimable = ifelse(grepl("^All", estimability), "all", estimability))],
             col.names = c("Fit", "Max |grad|, nlminb", "Max |grad|, final",
                           "Newton steps", "opal check", "Estimable"))
```

nlminb runs two passes. A few Newton steps then take the maximum gradient
below 1e-8, and `opal_check()` runs at a gradient tolerance of 1e-4,
checking the Hessian, bounds, population and estimability. Timings are from a
`r cache$session$cpu` machine with `r cache$session$cores` cores. The first
vignette found wall-clock times on this cloud container varying by up to 2×
between sessions with identical iteration counts, so treat the times as
indicative.

# Index fits

```{r}
#| label: index-fits
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Observed index (points, ±1.96 SE) with the fitted opal predictions and SS3's expected values, each quarterly series on a mean-one scale."
cp = cache$cpue
obs = cp[id == "A1", .(ts, fishery, obs, se)]
pred = rbind(cp[, .(ts, fishery, value = pred_fit, series = lab[id])],
             ss3$cpue[, .(ts, fishery, value = exp, series = lab["ss3"])])
ggplot() +
    geom_linerange(data = obs, aes(ts, ymin = obs * exp(-1.96 * se), ymax = obs * exp(1.96 * se)),
                   colour = "grey60") +
    geom_point(data = obs, aes(ts, obs), size = 1.1, colour = "grey40") +
    geom_line(data = pred, aes(ts, value, colour = series, linetype = series), linewidth = 0.6) +
    facet_wrap(~ fishery, ncol = 1, labeller = as_labeller(fleet_name)) +
    scale_series + guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2)) +
    labs(x = "Timestep (quarter)", y = "Index (mean = 1 per series)")
```

```{r}
#| label: index-stats
rmse = function(o, p) sqrt(mean((log(o) - log(p))^2))
knitr::kable(rbind(cp[, .(series = lab[id], rmse_log = rmse(obs, pred_fit)), by = id][, .(series, rmse_log)],
                   ss3$cpue[, .(series = lab["ss3"], rmse_log = rmse(obs, exp))]),
             digits = 4, col.names = c("Model", "RMSE of log residuals"))
```

# Composition fits

```{r}
#| label: comp-aggregate
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-cap: "Length compositions aggregated over all observations per fishery, weighted by effective sample size."
lf = merge(cache$lf, ss3$lf, by = c("ts", "fishery", "bin"), all.x = TRUE)
agg = lf[, .(obs = sum(obs * n), pred = sum(pred * n), ss3_pred = sum(ss3_pred * n)),
         by = .(id, fishery, bin)]
agg[, `:=`(obs = obs / sum(obs), pred = pred / sum(pred), ss3_pred = ss3_pred / sum(ss3_pred)),
    by = .(id, fishery)]
agg_pred = rbind(agg[id %in% c("A1", "C", "C2"), .(fishery, bin, value = pred, series = lab[id])],
                 agg[id == "A1", .(fishery, bin, value = ss3_pred, series = lab["ss3"])])
ggplot() +
    geom_col(data = agg[id == "A1"], aes(bin + 2.5, obs), fill = "grey80", width = 5) +
    geom_line(data = agg_pred, aes(bin + 2.5, value, colour = series, linetype = series), linewidth = 0.6) +
    facet_wrap(~ fishery, ncol = 4, scales = "free_y", labeller = as_labeller(fleet_name)) +
    scale_series +
    labs(x = "Length (cm)", y = "Proportion")
```

With SS3's growth, A1's predicted compositions sit on SS3's expectation; in
the first vignette, the Schnute curve pushed them to the right. Fit C's
predictions differ from SS3's only through selectivity.

```{r}
#| label: comp-nll
knitr::kable(S[, .(series = lab[id], lp_lf = round(lp_lf, 1), lp_cpue = round(lp_cpue, 1),
                   lp_rec = round(lp_rec, 1), lp_prior = round(lp_prior, 1))],
             col.names = c("Model", "NLL length comps", "NLL index", "Recruitment penalty", "Priors"))
```

The composition NLL is not comparable with SS3's, because opal's multinomial
keeps its normalising constant.

# Selectivity

```{r}
#| label: sel-age
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-cap: "Selectivity-at-age: SS3 (A1 and A2 use it unchanged), the seeded starting curves shared by C and C2, and the C and C2 estimates."
sa = rbind(ss3$sel_age[, .(fishery, age, sel, series = "SS3")],
           cache$sel_age[id == "C" & state == "start", .(fishery, age, sel, series = "opal C, seeded start")],
           cache$sel_age[id == "C" & state == "fitted", .(fishery, age, sel, series = "opal C, estimated")],
           cache$sel_age[id == "C2" & state == "fitted", .(fishery, age, sel, series = "opal C2, estimated")])
ggplot(sa[fishery <= 17], aes(age, sel, colour = series, linetype = series)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
    facet_wrap(~ fishery, ncol = 4, labeller = as_labeller(fleet_name)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("SS3" = "grey20", "opal C, seeded start" = "#A6ACAF",
                                   "opal C, estimated" = "#1E8449", "opal C2, estimated" = "#8E44AD"), name = NULL) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c("SS3" = "solid", "opal C, seeded start" = "dotted",
                                     "opal C, estimated" = "solid", "opal C2, estimated" = "dashed"), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Age (quarters)", y = "Selectivity")
```

Panels 15 and 16 mirror 14, and 17 stands for all four quarterly index series
(18–20 are identical). The seeded curves are SS3's selectivity projected onto
length and fitted with opal's length-based families. The estimated curves
show where the length compositions, read through opal's dynamics, pull them.

```{r}
#| label: sel-shift
ps = cache$par_sel[id == "C" & estimated == TRUE]
ps[, family := ifelse(fishery >= 17, "logistic", "double-normal")]
ps[, name := ifelse(family == "logistic", c("a50", "width")[col],
                    c("peak", "plateau", "ascending width", "descending width", "initial", "final")[col])]
knitr::kable(dcast(ps[fishery %in% c(1:14, 17)], fishery ~ name, value.var = "fit")[
    , c("fishery", "peak", "plateau", "ascending width", "descending width", "a50", "width"), with = FALSE],
    digits = 2, col.names = c("Fishery", "Peak", "Plateau", "Asc. width", "Desc. width", "a50", "Width"))
```

The table gives fitted values on opal's parameter scale (positions in units
of sd(len_mid) about mean(len_mid), widths on the log scale). None sits at
opal's default bound of ±7.

**Several estimates are set by the prior, not the data.** opal places a
N(0, 2) prior on every `par_sel` value. A parameter that the length
compositions cannot inform settles at the prior mean of 0.

```{r}
#| label: sel-prior
ps_all = cache$par_sel[id == "C" & estimated == TRUE & fishery %in% c(1:14, 17)]
ps_all[, name := ifelse(fishery >= 17, c("a50", "width")[col],
                        c("peak", "plateau", "ascending width", "descending width")[col])]
flag = ps_all[abs(fit) < 0.05 & abs(start) > 0.25]
knitr::kable(flag[, .(fishery = fleet_name(fishery), parameter = name, start, fit)],
             digits = 3, col.names = c("Fishery", "Parameter", "Seeded start", "Estimate"))
```

These `r nrow(flag)` parameters moved from their seeded values to within
0.05 of zero. For the asymptotic fisheries (4, 5, 7, 13) they are the plateau
and descending width, the whole right-hand side of the curve. Selectivity
there has reached 1 before the largest lengths observed, so the data say
nothing about where a descending limb would start. Fishery 9's descending
width goes the same way, and its plateau moves from
`r fmt(ps_all[fishery == 9 & name == "plateau", start], 2)` to
`r fmt(ps_all[fishery == 9 & name == "plateau", fit], 2)`, which is why its
curve stays flat and then drops at the largest ages. SS3 estimated the
corresponding parameters too, without a prior. In opal they are estimable
(the Hessian is positive definite and `opal_check()` passes) only because of
the prior.

The priors also explain why fit C has a higher total objective than A1
despite fitting the data better. They add
`r fmt(S[id == "C", lp_prior] - S[id == "A1", lp_prior], 0)` units relative to
A1, more than the
`r fmt(S[id == "C", objective_fit] - S[id == "A1", objective_fit], 0)`-unit
difference in total. Without them, C's composition NLL is
`r fmt(S[id == "A1", lp_lf] - S[id == "C", lp_lf], 1)` lower than A1's, with
the index and recruitment terms almost unchanged.

The survey logistic (fishery 17) also barely moved from its seeded start,
since opal's only information on it is the index itself.

## Fit C2: the prior-dominated parameters fixed

Fit C2 repeats C with those nine parameters held at their seeded values,
the opal curves fitted to SS3's selectivity, and estimates the other
`r S[id == "C2", n_par_sel]`.

```{r}
#| label: c2
c2_sel = dcast(cache$sel_age[id %in% c("C", "C2") & state == "fitted"], fishery + age ~ id,
               value.var = "sel")
c2_pars = merge(cache$par_sel[id == "C2" & estimated == TRUE, .(fishery, col, fit_C2 = fit)],
                cache$par_sel[id == "C", .(fishery, col, fit_C = fit)], by = c("fishery", "col"))
fixed_prior = cache$par_sel[id == "C2" & estimated == FALSE][
    flag[, .(fishery, col)], on = c("fishery", "col")][, sum((fit / 2)^2 / 2)]
knitr::kable(data.table(
    quantity = c("Objective", "NLL length comps", "NLL index", "Recruitment penalty", "Priors",
                 "B0 (t)", "Terminal SSB/B0"),
    C  = c(S[id == "C",  objective_fit], S[id == "C",  lp_lf], S[id == "C",  lp_cpue],
           S[id == "C",  lp_rec], S[id == "C",  lp_prior], S[id == "C",  B0_fit],
           term(tr[id == "C"], "static_dep")),
    C2 = c(S[id == "C2", objective_fit], S[id == "C2", lp_lf], S[id == "C2", lp_cpue],
           S[id == "C2", lp_rec], S[id == "C2", lp_prior], S[id == "C2", B0_fit],
           term(tr[id == "C2"], "static_dep"))),
    digits = 3, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), col.names = c("Quantity", "C", "C2"))
```

**C2 is the same fit as C.** The likelihood components agree to the third
decimal, B0 differs by
`r fmt(100 * abs(S[id == "C2", B0_fit] / S[id == "C", B0_fit] - 1), 3)`%, and the
other estimated selectivity parameters move by at most
`r fmt(max(abs(c2_pars$fit_C2 - c2_pars$fit_C)), 3)`. The selectivity curves
differ by at most `r fmt(max(abs(c2_sel$C2 - c2_sel$C)), 3)` (fishery
`r c2_sel[which.max(abs(C2 - C)), fishery]` at age
`r c2_sel[which.max(abs(C2 - C)), age]`, the plus group) and by under 1e-4
everywhere else. The only difference in the objective is the prior: opal's
N(0, 2) prior still applies to the fixed values, which adds a constant
`r fmt(fixed_prior, 2)` units, exactly the
`r fmt(S[id == "C2", lp_prior] - S[id == "C", lp_prior], 2)` difference in the
prior term.

This confirms that those nine parameters are unidentified by the data. The
likelihood is flat in them, so it makes no difference whether the prior or a
fixed value sets them. It also shows that C's lower stock size (B0
`r fmt(S[id == "C", B0_fit] / ss3$ssb0, 2)` × SS3's, against A1's
`r fmt(S[id == "A1", B0_fit] / ss3$ssb0, 2)` ×) comes from the selectivity
parameters the length compositions *do* inform, not from the prior. Fixing
the unidentified parameters is the cleaner configuration: the selectivity
parameters in C2 are all informed by the data, and the result does not
depend on the prior.

```{r}
p1 = ggplot(all_traj, aes(ts, ssb / 1e6, colour = series, linetype = series)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) + scale_series +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Spawning biomass (millions t)")
p2 = ggplot(all_traj, aes(ts, static_dep, colour = series, linetype = series)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) + scale_series + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, NA)) +
    labs(x = "Timestep (quarter)", y = "SSB / B0")
patchwork::wrap_plots(p1, p2, ncol = 1, guides = "collect") &
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") & guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2))
```

```{r}
#| label: recruitment
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Recruitment deviations: opal fits against SS3's. opal's deviation for timestep t sets the age-1 recruits entering at t + 1."
rd = merge(cache$parameters, ss3$recdevs[, .(ts = year, ss3 = recdev)], by = "ts")
ggplot(rd, aes(ss3, rdev_fit, colour = lab[id])) +
    geom_abline(colour = "grey60") +
    geom_point(size = 0.7, alpha = 0.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = col, name = NULL) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2)) +
    labs(x = "SS3 recruitment deviation", y = "opal recruitment deviation")
```

## Against SS3 and against the truth

```{r}
#| label: comparison-table
models = list(A1 = tr[id == "A1"], A2 = tr[id == "A2"], C = tr[id == "C"], C2 = tr[id == "C2"],
              schnute = sch, ss3 = ss3$trajectory)
b0 = c(A1 = S[id == "A1", B0_fit], A2 = S[id == "A2", B0_fit], C = S[id == "C", B0_fit],
       C2 = S[id == "C2", B0_fit],
       schnute = cache$schnute$summary[route == "endgrowth", B0_fit], ss3 = ss3$ssb0)
cmp = rbindlist(lapply(names(models), function(k) {
    a = if (k == "ss3") NULL else vs(models[[k]], ss3$trajectory)
    b = vs(models[[k]], truth_traj)
    data.table(model = lab[k], B0_ss3 = b0[[k]] / ss3$ssb0, B0_truth = b0[[k]] / truth$b0,
               ssb_mean_ss3 = if (is.null(a)) NA_real_ else a$mean_abs_pct,
               ssb_mean_truth = b$mean_abs_pct, terminal_dep = b$terminal_dep,
               dep_err_truth = b$max_dep_err)
}))
cmp = rbind(cmp, data.table(model = lab["truth"], B0_ss3 = truth$b0 / ss3$ssb0, B0_truth = 1,
                            terminal_dep = term(truth_traj, "static_dep")), fill = TRUE)
knitr::kable(cmp, digits = c(0, 2, 2, 1, 1, 3, 3),
             col.names = c("Model", "B0 / SS3 B0", "B0 / true B0", "SSB mean |% diff| from SS3",
                           "SSB mean |% diff| from truth", "Terminal SSB/B0",
                           "Max |depletion error| vs truth"))
```

# Remaining differences from SS3

With growth reproduced, the structural differences between these opal fits
and SS3 are the ones measured in the first vignette:

* **Catch timing.** opal removes each quarter's catch at the start of the
  step; SS3 uses Baranov catch through the step (`F_Method = 3`). At SS3's
  parameter values this alone moves opal's SSB by up to 10%.
* **Spawner-recruit timing.** opal's first age class at t + 1 comes from SSB
  at t + 1; SS3's age-0 recruits at t come from SSB at t.
* **Index.** opal fits the longline index as four quarterly series with four
  catchabilities, against abundance at the start of the step. SS3 fits one
  series with one analytic q, sampled mid-season.
* **Size-frequency data.** SS3's generalised size compositions for the survey
  (λ = 0.51) are not converted.
* **Plus-group equilibrium.** SS3 iterates it to 3 × Nages; opal uses the
  geometric tail. This makes a difference of about 5e-5 in SPR0.
* **Selectivity (fits C and C2).** opal's curves are length-based and map to age
  through the PLA; SS3's are age-based. Both use the same growth here, so the
  difference is in curve shape, not in the age-length key.

# Credit

The baseline SS3 model (`case-studies/io-yft/model-files/ss3/xx-io-yft-sim-iattc-sample-tree-4`)
was developed by the IATTC analyst team for the Spatial Stock Assessment Simulation Experiment: Mark N. Maunder, Haikun Xu and Carolina Minte-Vera (Inter-American Tropical Tuna Commission). The yellowfin assessments from the experiment,
including theirs, are evaluated in Goethel, D.R., et al. (2024). 'Drivin' with your eyes closed': Results from an international, blinded simulation experiment to evaluate spatial stock assessments. *Fish and Fisheries* 25(3): 471–490. <https://doi.org/10.1111/faf.12819>

The age-specific K growth model is Stock Synthesis' `GrowthModel 3` (Methot,
R.D. Jr., and Wetzel, C.R. 2013. Stock synthesis: A biological and statistical
framework for fish stock assessment and fishery management. *Fisheries
Research* 142: 86–99. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fishres.2012.10.012>;
source: <https://github.com/nmfs-ost/ss3-source-code>). It is implemented in
opal from version 0.1.1.

The data and the simulated truth come from replicate 4 of the Indian Ocean
yellowfin operating model of the
[Spatial Stock Assessment Simulation Experiment](https://aaronmberger-nwfsc.github.io/Spatial-Assessment-Modeling-Workshop/)
(repository
<https://github.com/aaronmberger-nwfsc/Spatial-Assessment-Modeling-Workshop>).
That operating model was built in SPM (Dunn, Rasmussen and Mormede 2015),
based on Dunn, Hoyle and Datta (2020), with growth from Fu et al. (2018) after
Fonteneau and Gascuel (2008). See
`case-studies/io-yft/model-files/sim-truth/io-yft-iattc-sample-tree-4/README.md` for file
provenance.
